一支警察搜查队正准备拦停一辆汽车时，
该汽车突然加速，车内人员向
警察开了两枪。
警察还击。
一名路人受伤。

page_data.en:
At 7.20 p.m. 12/12/39, Prob. Sgt. 713 J.
Nagishi in charge of a search party consisting of
C.P.C.1861, C.P.C.1891 and C.P.C.1894, came to the
station, and reported that whilst about to stop a
passing car, he and his party had been fired upon by
the occupants of the car, who, despite a return of
fire, had escaped.

P.S. Nagishi stated:-

At 7.15 p.m. 12/12/39 he and his party were on
the south side of Avenue Road, a short distance west
of Hardoon Road. At this time, a m/car was seen
approaching from the east, and P.S. Nagishi decided
to search it. He therefore stood out in the road,
and raised his hand to the oncoming car. The car
began to slow down, and P.S. Nagishi moved to the
near side of the road. As he did this, the car
started to accelerate. P.S. Nagishi noticed that
the car occupants were five Chinese male persons, and
as the car passed him, the person sitting in the rear
nearside seat, opened fire through the closed window.
Two shots were fired at the police party.

(P.S. Nagishi discovered at the station that
a bullet had passed under his right armpit. The
cloth of his jacket was damaged, but the flesh was
only slightly bruised).

The police party at once returned the fire.
P.S. Nagishi fired 6 shots, C.P.C.1861 one shot,
C.P.C.1891 one shot, and C.P.C.1894 two shots.

The car moved off at a very fast rate, without
lights, and disappeared west along Avenue Road.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

At 10a.m. on the 16-12-39 an attempted murder took place in passage No. 42 Route de Zay Zoong. Three cartridge cases and 1 bullet found at the scene proved upon examination to have been fired from the same pistols as those used by the culprits who perpetrated the crime which is the subject of this F.I.R.

Detectives have made careful and discreet enquiries re the character, haunts and associates of the female named Chung Wong Sz residing at 27/41 Sing Ping Street who reported to Chengtu Road Station that her chauffeur Nyi Ching Sang had taken away her motor-car license No. 3446, (Chengtu Road F.I.R. 1787/39) but nothing could be elicited which would connect her in any way with this offence, or any political activities.

All efforts to locate other two individuals named (1) Chang Tong Ching and (2) Tsu Moh Ching who were suspected to have knowledge of this affair, has met with no success.

As per attached diaries, every channel of enquiry that this case has presented itself has been followed up, with negative results. In view of the foregoing coupled with the fact that there is no other line of enquiry that can be taken up, or any information available on which to base further investigations this case is respectfully submitted for classification pending further developments which may arise.

DEC 1 8 1939

What About 76 Jessfield Road?
THE DEATH of Miss Mao Li-ying as result
of assassins' bullets makes the circum-
stances of the attack upon her last Tuesday
night additionally grave.
This well known social worker and teacher
fell victim to shots fired by two Chinese thugs
who escaped in a black motorcar. After a subse-
quent brush with police in Avenue Road, when
an S.M.P. party endeavored to halt the vehicle
for inspection, this car was seen driving into
the headquarters of Mr. Wang Ching-wei's
local organization at 76 Jessfield Road.
Additional evidence was subsequently
afforded when it was learned, through expert
examination of the empty cartridge cases
taken at the scene of the attack upon Miss
Mao, that the shots were fired from a gun in
possession of a Chinese who is understood to
be living at 76 Jessfield Road.
In revealing these facts a few days ago our
contemporary the North-China Daily News
drew one more line of evidence, pointing out
that two men were arrested last July after they
had attempted to stop a charity bazaar con-
ducted by Miss Mao. When they appeared in
the First Special District Court they gave their
address as 76 Jessfield Road. (It develops that
they were sentenced to serve seven months in
jail but for reasons not disclosed, the sentences
were suspended and the pair went free at the
beginning of September.)
Taking all these facts into consideration,
it would seem the conclusion of any impartial
law-abiding person that an immediate inves-
tigation of the premises at 76 Jessfield Road
would be decidedly in order.
Why cannot this be done? It goes back to
Shanghai's extraordinary constitution, plus the
special conditions now prevailing. But that
does not necessarily give a final answer.
Jessfield Road is an extra-Settlement
highway running through Chinese territory.
In normal times this territory is under control
of the Chinese municipal government. Today
the Japanese-sponsored "City Government"
claims control but actually leaves it a no-man's
land from which it draws revenue but upon
which it confers nothing in the way of
administration except as regards the gambling
and other rackets, which have to obtain
official licenses. The Japanese army collabora-
tes in this nefarious situation.

But Jessfield Road and the rest of the
"badlands" is within the foreign defense sector
and, not for the first time, we urge upon the
military authorities the scandalousness of this
whole situation.
Can immunity be conferred upon such a
den as 76 Jessfield Road appears to be without
shame to every military commander, including
or especially the Japanese? We say NO. To
allow a pack of armed and desperate
characters, in this latest assassination definite-
ly linked with murder, to hold a fort inside the
defense sector is intolerable. No excuse
whatever can be urged from any quarter save
the excuse of sheerest expediency.
There is every reason why pointed ques-
tions should be put to all who stand in the
way of a shake-up of this whole situation. Two
obviously indicated recipients of such queries
are Mayor Fu Siao-en of the City Government
and the Japanese military.
To Mayor Fu, the case might be put that
he professes to wish to function as a real
municipal executive, not as a puppet. Is there
the slightest possible explanation for not con-
ducting, or at least collaborating in, a raid on
76 Jessfield Road forthwith under the circum-
stances already outlined which trace
responsibility for the murder of Miss Mao Li-
ying directly to this place?
To the Japanese military, it may be asked
whether there is the slightest compatibility
between their insistent demands for peace and
order, and their failure to move against 76
Jessfield Road or to see that others are allowed
to do so.
The plain fact is that the strongest of
evidence indicates 76 Jessfield Road to be
something worse than a robbers' roost. How
much longer is it to be permitted to harbor
and to send forth gunmen bent on political
assassination?

1939年12月18日

极司菲尔路76号怎么了？
毛丽英小姐死于刺客枪下，使得上周二晚
上对她的袭击情节更加严重。
这位著名的社会工作者和教师成为了两名
中国暴徒枪击的受害者，这两人乘一辆黑色汽
车逃逸。随后在大西路与警察发生短暂交火，当时
上海公共租界警务处的一支小队试图拦停该车辆
进行检查，人们看到这辆汽车驶入了汪精卫先生
地方组织的总部，地址为极司菲尔路76号。
随后又提供了更多证据，据获悉，通过对
毛小姐遇袭现场提取的空弹壳进行专家检验，
确认开枪所用的枪支属于一名据信居住在
极司菲尔路76号的华人。

几天前，我们的同行《字林西报》在披露这些事实时
又提供了一条证据线索，指出去年七月有两人因
试图阻止毛小姐举办的慈善义卖而被捕。当他们在
第一特区法院出庭时，他们提供的地址是极司菲尔路76号。（据悉，
他们被判入狱七个月，但由于未公开的原因，判决
被暂缓执行，这两人在九月初获释。）

考虑到所有这些事实，任何公正守法的人似乎都会得出
这样的结论：立即调查极司菲尔路76号的 premises
绝对是合乎情理的。

为什么不能这样做？这要归咎于上海特殊的体制，加上
当前 prevailing 的特殊条件。但这并不一定给出最终答案。
极司菲尔路是一条穿过中国领土的租界外道路。
在正常时期，这片领土由中国市政府控制。如今，
日本扶植的“市政府”声称拥有控制权，但实际上将其留为
无人地带，从中抽取收入，但在行政方面除了
赌博和其他勒索活动需要获得官方许可外，
不提供任何服务。日本军队在这种邪恶的局面中予以配合。

但是，极司菲尔路及其余的“不良地带”位于
外国防区内，我们并非第一次向军事当局强调
整个局面的丑恶性质。

难道可以毫无羞耻地赋予像极司菲尔路76号这样的
巢穴以豁免权吗，这对每一位军事指挥官，包括
尤其是日本指挥官来说，难道不是耻辱吗？我们要说：不。允许一伙武装且绝望的
人物，在这次明确与谋杀有关的最新暗杀事件中，
在防区内占据一个据点，这是不可容忍的。除了
纯粹的权宜之计这一借口外，任何一方都提不出
任何借口。

完全有理由向所有阻碍彻底整顿这一局面的人
提出尖锐的问题。两个显然应当接受此类质询的对象
是“市政府”市长傅筱庵和日本军方。

对傅市长，可以这样质问：他声称希望作为一个真正的
市政行政长官行事，而不是作为傀儡。在目前概述的情况下，
已有证据直接将毛丽英小姐被谋杀的责任追溯到此地，
如果不立即对极司菲尔路76号进行突袭，或者至少参与合作，
哪怕有一丝可能的解释吗？

对日本军方，可以质问：他们坚持要求和平与
秩序，却不对极司菲尔路76号采取行动，或允许他人
这样做，这两者之间哪怕有一丝兼容性吗？

显而易见的事实是，最有力的证据表明极司菲尔路76号
不仅仅是强盗的巢穴。还要允许它藏匿并派出
致力于政治暗杀的枪手多久？

December 18, 1939. Morning Translation.
Ta Mei Pao (Editorial) :-
76 JESSFIELD ROAD
The murder of Miss Mao Lien-ying (茅丽英 ),
an educationist, is a matter of a very serious nature. The
death of this social worker was brought about by desperadoes
who after the crime decamped in a private motor car. It
is said that when the car passed by Avenue Road, its
occupants were involved in a shooting affray with Settlement
Police after which the car was driven off towards No. 76
Jessfield Road, the headquarters of Wang Ching-wei.
Later according to an examination by ballistic
experts, cartridges left behind by the desperadoes were
shown to have been fired from a pistol belonging to a
Chinese residing at No. 76 Jessfield Road.
According to the "North China Daily News," two
Chinese were arrested some time in July this year for
interference with the Charity Sales Exhibition promoted by
the late Miss Mao and when arraigned before the Shanghai
First Special District Court, stated that they resided at
No. 76 Jessfield Road. (these two men were given a
suspended sentence of seven months imprisonment, being
released at the beginning of September.)
In view of the foregoing, it appears obvious
to law-abiding citizens that a search should be made at the
address mentioned without delay. Why should it not be
possible to carry out such a search? Due to the extra-
ordinary circumstances, such an action may present
difficulties, but should not be considered impossible.
Jessfield Road lies in the extra-Settlement
roads area and extends through Chinese territory. In
former times, it was under the jurisdiction of the Chinese
municipal government. Now it is under the control of the
Japanese sponsored City Government which claims to have
the right to exercise jurisdiction. In reality, it has now
become an area without authority. The City Government is
now doing its utmost to enforce the collection of rates and
taxes in the area, but so far has done nothing to improve
the administrative affairs of the district, except for
establishing a number of gambling and opium dens. The
Japanese military authorities are said to have extended
their co-operation in the toleration of these vices.
However, Jessfield Road and other areas of the "badlands"
all lie within the defence sectors of the foreign defence
forces. We have on several occasions called the attention
of the local military authorities to the existence of such
vices.
Plainly speaking, the organ established at
No. 76 Jessfield Road should receive no consideration from
the commanders of the foreign defence forces, especially
the Japanese. Under the circumstances, is it just to give
immunity to No. 76 Jessfield Road?
We have now the following questions to put to
Mayor Fu Siao-en and the Japanese military authorities:-
(1) Since the Mayor has claimed that he is not
a puppet but a genuine executive official in municipal
affairs, why has he failed to carry out a raid or to assist
the Settlement authorities to do so at No. 76 Jessfield Road?
(2) From the viewpoint of the Japanese military
authorities, since they have made repeated request for the
maintenance of peace and order, why have they themselves
failed to bring about the suppression of the activities
carried on at No. 76 Jessfield Road and refused the request
of others, denying them the right to carry out the suppression
of this den of vice?

极司菲尔路76号
教育家茅丽英女士被谋杀一案，性质极为严重。这位社会工作者的死亡是由歹徒造成的，作案后歹徒乘私家车逃逸。据说，当该车经过爱文义路时，车内人员与租界警察发生枪战，随后车辆驶向极司菲尔路76号，即汪精卫的总部。
后来据弹道专家检验，歹徒留下的子弹经鉴定系从一名居住在极司菲尔路76号的中国人所有的手枪中射出。
据《字林西报》报道，今年7月间，两名中国人因干扰已故茅女士倡导的慈善义卖展览会而被捕，他们在上海第一特区地方法院受审时声称居住在极司菲尔路76号。（这两人被判处七个月徒刑，缓期执行，于9月初获释。）
鉴于上述情况，守法公民显然认为应立即搜查上述地址。为何不能进行此类搜查？由于情况特殊，此类行动可能会遇到困难，但不应被视为不可能。
极司菲尔路位于越界筑路区域，并穿过中国领土。过去，它由中国市政府管辖。现在，它由日本扶持的市政府控制，该政府声称拥有行使管辖权的权利。实际上，它现在已成为一个无政府管辖的区域。市政府目前正竭尽全力在该区域征收捐税，但除了设立一些赌场和鸦片馆外，至今未在该区行政事务方面做任何改善工作。据说日本军方当局在容忍这些恶习方面给予了合作。
然而，极司菲尔路和其他“坏地带”区域均位于外国驻军的防区内。我们曾多次提请当地军事当局注意此类恶习的存在。
坦率地说，设在极司菲尔路76号的机构不应得到外国驻军指挥官，特别是日本指挥官的任何关照。在这种情况下，给予极司菲尔路76号豁免权是否公正？
我们现在向市长傅筱庵和日本军事当局提出以下问题：-
(1) 既然市长声称自己不是傀儡，而是市政事务中真正的行政官员，为何他未能对极司菲尔路76号进行突击搜查，或协助租界当局进行搜查？
(2) 从日本军事当局的角度来看，既然他们反复要求维持治安，为何他们自己未能镇压在极司菲尔路76号进行的活动，并拒绝他人的请求，剥夺他人镇压这一罪恶巢穴的权利？

CHINA PRESS.

DEC 16 1939

Teacher Dies
From Thugs'
Shot Wounds

By GEORGE LEONOF
Unable in her weakened condition to continue her battle against death, Miss Mao Li-ying, 28-year-old school teacher who was shot down by assassins' bullets Tuesday night, succumbed to her wounds at the Lester Chinese Hospital at 2.15 p.m. yesterday.

Reports on Wednesday that Miss Mao was recovering were due to a slight improvement in her condition. She was too weak to survive a subsequent relapse, however. Death was caused by a fatal wound in the abdomen on which a delicate operation was performed Wednesday morning.

Meanwhile, Japanese authorities made no attempt to co-operate with the Shanghai Municipal Police in identifying the assassins. Strong circumstantial evidence, consisting of an inseparable sequence of events Tuesday night pointed to 76 Jessfield Road, notorious headquarters of Wang Ching-wei's "bodyguards," as the home of the assassins.

Fail To Investigate
Japanese authorities have assured the S.M.P. that they would investigate the matter, but up to last night no action on their part had been announced.

Miss Mao, known to be a strong sympathizer of the Chungking Government, was shot down by two assassins shortly before 7 p.m. Tuesday, as she stepped out on Nanking Road from the Shanghai Vocational Chinese Women's Lien Nyi Society, at 130 Nanking Road, adjoining the Hall and Holtz Building.

Miss Mao was employed as a teacher at the Chi Siu Middle School for Girls on Avenue Joffre, near Rue Massenet, and for some time had been receiving warnings and threatening letters.

As far back as last July police here arrested two men who had been sent to close a charity bazaar conducted by Miss Mao.

Admit Connection
When these men appeared before the First Special District Court they gave their common address as 76 Jessfield Road, hang-out of the notorious Wang Ching-wei "bodyguards" who recently figured in several armed clashes with the S.M.P. The men were each sentenced to seven months' imprisonment—a sentence later suspended.

All available evidence points in a common direction—76 Jessfield Road. It is known that immediately following Miss Mao's assassination two Chinese were seen running northwards along Szechuen Road from the Nanking Road intersection. Turning into Ningpo Road, they jumped into a waiting black limousine which immediately started off in a westerly direction.

At approximately 7:15 p.m. a black limousine, traveling west along Avenue Road with all lights doused, failed to stop when ordered by a police search party near Hart Road. Instead, the car gathered speed and the occupants opened fire on the police, who replied.

Crawls Into Headquarters
Shortly before 7:30 p.m. a black limousine was seen crawling into 76 Jessfield Road with a flat tire. Immediately the armed guard outside the gate was reinforced by other armed men.

While it is pointed out that these facts, albeit inseparable, are not strictly conclusive evidence, it was said that the allegation offered by this sequence of events cannot be dispelled unless by a thorough investigation.

教师死于
暴徒枪伤

乔治·列昂诺夫 著

这位28岁的学校女教师茅丽英小姐在周二晚遭刺客枪击，因身体虚弱无法继续与死神抗争，于昨日下午2时15分在莱斯德华人医院伤重不治。

周三有关茅小姐正在康复的报道是由于其病情略有好转。然而，她身体过于虚弱，无法挺过随后的病情恶化。死因是腹部的一处致命伤，周三上午对此进行了精细的手术。

与此同时，日本当局并未尝试与上海公共租界工部局警务处合作识别刺客。强有力的间接证据，由周二晚上一系列不可分割的事件组成，指向极司菲尔路76号，即汪精卫“保镖”的臭名昭著的总部，作为刺客的藏身之处。

未能调查
日本当局已向工部局警务处保证将调查此事，但截至昨晚，尚未宣布采取任何行动。

茅小姐众所周知是重庆政府的坚定同情者，周二晚上7点前不久，当她从位于南京路130号、毗邻霍尔和霍尔茨大楼的上海职业妇女俱乐部走出到南京路上时，被两名刺客枪击。

茅小姐受雇于靠近马思南路的霞飞路启秀女子中学担任教师，并在一段时间内一直收到警告信和恐吓信。

早在去年7月，本地警方就逮捕了两名被派去关闭由茅小姐举办的慈善义卖会的男子。

承认关联
当这些人在第一特区地方法院出庭时，他们提供的共同住址是极司菲尔路76号，这是臭名昭著的汪精卫“保镖”的聚集地，他们最近多次与工部局警务处发生武装冲突。这些人各被判处七个月监禁——该判决后来被缓期执行。

所有现有证据都指向同一个方向——极司菲尔路76号。据悉，在茅小姐遇刺后不久，有人看到两名中国人从南京路交叉口沿四川路向北奔跑。转入宁波路后，他们跳进一辆等候的黑色豪华轿车，该车随即向西驶去。

大约晚上7点15分，一辆黑色豪华轿车沿爱文义路向西行驶，所有车灯熄灭，在哈特路附近被警察搜索队命令停车时未予理睬。相反，汽车加速，车内人员向警察开火，警察予以还击。

爬进总部
晚上7点30分前不久，有人看到一辆爆胎的黑色豪华轿车缓慢驶入极司菲尔路76号。大门外的武装警卫立即得到其他武装人员的增援。

虽然指出这些事实尽管紧密相连，但并非严格意义上的确凿证据，但据说，除非进行彻底调查，否则无法消除由这一系列事件提出的指控。

DEC 1 3 1939

Attack On Social
Worker Angers
Local Socialites

Four Shots Fired By
Gunmen; Victim In
Serious Condition

A wave of indignation swept
Chinese social circles this morning
in connection with the dastardly
attack by two gunmen upon Miss
Mao Li-ying, 28, a well known local
social and charitable worker and
the head of the Shanghai Profes-
sional Woman's Club, 120 Nanking
Road.

Miss Mao was attacked at 6.10
yesterday afternoon while, together
with several members of the club,
she was leaving the club premises.

Four shots were fired by the
assassins and Miss Mao was wound-
ed in the abdomen and in the leg.
The gunmen were seen by two
foreign ladies who were passing by
at the time of the attack, who re-
ported to the police that they saw
them run towards Peking Road
along Szechuen Road.

Meanwhile, Miss Mao is still fight-
ing for her life in a hospital and
although her condition is described
as serious it is believed that she
will live.

Came From Badlands

The gunmen came from the
Western district Badlands, according
to the Police authorities and poli-
tical motives were believed to be
behind the crime. Miss Mao, who
was very popular amongst the
Chinese women's sections, was re-
ported to be a strong Chungking
sympathiser.

Several Cartridge cases which
came from the 32 calibre auto-
matics used by the gunmen were
being examined by the ballistic
experts of the Shanghai Municipal
Police this morning in order to
determine whether or not the same
guns had been used in other armed
crimes committed by the Badlands
gangsters in the Settlement.

Escapes By Sheer Luck

The authorities believe that only
sheer luck helped the gunmen to
escape from the custody of the law.
The black limousine which was in-
volved in an exchange of shots with
a party of Chinese constables con-
ducting a routine search patrol
along Avenue Road, near Hart Road,
a short time after the attempt on
Miss Mao's life, is believed to have
been the getaway car of the gun-
men. The C.P.C. succeeded in
disabling the car to a certain
extent, but it managed to get away
in spite of a flat tyre. Detectives
from the Central Police station are
today busy investigating various
angles of the latest outrages com-
mitted by the Badlands gangsters
in the heart of the business centre
of the Settlement.

1939年12月13日

袭击社会工作者
激怒本地社交名流

枪手连开四枪；受害者
情况危急

今晨，两名枪手对知名本地社会及慈善工作者、上海职业妇女俱乐部主席茅丽瑛女士（28岁，俱乐部位于南京路120号）实施卑鄙袭击，此事在中国社交界激起了一阵愤怒浪潮。

昨日下午6时10分，茅女士与俱乐部数名成员一同离开俱乐部场所时遭到袭击。

刺客开了四枪，茅女士腹部和腿部中弹。两名当时路过的外国女士目睹了枪手，并向警方报告称，看到他们沿四川路向北京路方向逃窜。

与此同时，茅女士仍在医院里与死神搏斗，虽然其状况被描述为危重，但据信她能够存活。

来自“歹土”

据警方当局称，枪手来自西区“歹土”（Badlands，指法租界边缘治安混乱区域），据信这起犯罪背后有政治动机。茅女士在中国妇女群体中颇受欢迎，据报道她是重庆方面的强烈同情者。

上海公共租界警务处的弹道专家今晨正在检查枪手使用的.32口径自动手枪留下的几个弹壳，以确定这些枪支是否曾被“歹土”帮匪在租界内犯下的其他武装犯罪所使用。

侥幸逃脱

当局认为，枪手之所以能逃脱法律制裁，纯属侥幸。在企图杀害茅女士后不久，一辆黑色豪华轿车在哈特路（Hart Road）附近的爱文义路（Avenue Road）上，与正在进行例行搜索巡逻的一队中国巡捕发生交火。据信这辆车是枪手的逃逸车辆。中国巡捕队（C.P.C.）成功使该车受到一定程度的损坏，但尽管轮胎爆裂，车辆仍设法逃离。中央捕房的侦探们今天正忙于调查“歹土”帮匪在租界商业中心腹地犯下的最新暴行的各个方面。

My name is Kung Ping Shih ( 龔冰若 ), age 30,

我是上海中国妇女职业联谊会（中国职业妇女俱乐部）的发起人之一，该会现位于南京路120号203室。我现为该会的候补委员。我不是妇女救国会的成员，也不认识该运动的任何成员。

Zah Ling (石麟), female.
Ningpo
Sp.Br. Hqrs.           12/12/39

My name is Zah Ling (石麟). I am a native
of Ningpo, single, age 27. I am employed as an
accountant in the Yuan Foong (源丰) Shipping Hong,
Lane 51, 18 Kiangse Road, and residing at House 99 Paris
Terrace, Avenue Dubail. I am at present a member of the
executive committee of the Shanghai Vocational Chinese
Women's Lien Nyi Society, also known as China Business
Girls' Club, Room 203, 120 Nanking Road.
At 5.45 p.m. on December 12, 1939, I arrived at the
club office, Room 203, 120 Nanking Road, for the purpose
of attending a meeting to discuss preparations for the
holding of a concert on December 16 in the Chinese Y.M.C.A.,
123 Boulevard de Montigny. Eight persons were present
at the meeting, including Miss Mao Li-ying (茅麗英) and
Miss Kung Ping-shih (龔冰菱). When the meeting was
over at about 7 p.m., Miss Mao and Miss Kung and I went
downstairs in the lift. On getting out of the lift on
the ground floor we commenced to walk towards the street
(Nanking Road) but while we were still in the gateway leading
to Nanking Road (I was walking in the middle, Miss Mao on
right hand side and Miss Kung on the left, with a short
distance between each of us), two male Chinese, one of
whom was in foreign dress, colour not clear, approached us
and told us to "walk slowly". I then looked at the two men
and saw the one in foreign dress push me and Miss Mao
and prevented us from going ahead. He is about 5' 7" tall,
slim build, face not recognized, and had a pistol in his hand.

石麟 (Zah Ling)，女。
宁波
特别处总部           1939年12月12日

我叫石麟 (Zah Ling)。我是宁波人，未婚，27岁。我在江西路18号51弄源丰 (Yuan Foong) 航运商行担任会计，居住在杜美路 (Avenue Dubail) 巴黎公寓 (Paris Terrace) 99号。我目前是上海职业妇女联谊社（又称中国女子商业俱乐部，China Business Girls' Club）执行委员会的成员，该社位于南京路120号203室。
1939年12月12日下午5时45分，我到达南京路120号203室的俱乐部办公室，目的是参加一次会议，讨论为12月16日在莫利爱路 (Boulevard de Montigny) 123号中华基督教青年会举行音乐会的筹备工作。出席会议的有八人，包括茅丽英 (Mao Li-ying) 小姐和龚冰菱 (Kung Ping-shih) 小姐。会议于晚上7点左右结束后，茅小姐、龚小姐和我乘电梯下楼。当我们在一楼走出电梯时，开始向街道（南京路）走去，但当我们还在通往南京路的门道内时（我走在中间，茅小姐在右侧，龚小姐在左侧，彼此间距离不远），两名中国男子向我们走近，其中一人身穿西式服装，肤色不清，并叫我们“走慢点”。我当时看着这两名男子，看见那个穿西装的人推搡我和茅小姐，阻止我们前行。他身高约5英尺7英寸，身材瘦削，面容无法辨认，手中持有一把手枪。

- 2 -

I did not notice the other assailant. At this moment,
Miss Mao and I turned back towards the inside of the building
but before reaching the corridor leading to the lift, I
heard two or three shorts being fired and I saw Miss Mao
fall to the ground at the end of the gateway opposite the
door to the lift. I made good my escape into the corridor
and took shelter in the Hwa Hwa (華華) Magazine Company,
inside the building. I do not know what happened
afterwards. While I was in the Hwa Hwa Magazine Company,
I requested one of the staff of the company to telephone
to the Police Station reporting the shooting. After
remaining inside for about 10 minutes, I went out and
discovered Miss Mao lying on the ground floor at the foot
of the staircase next to the lift and by that time the
Police had arrived on the scene.

- 2 -

我没有注意到另一名袭击者。此时，
茅小姐和我转身向建筑物内部走去，但在到达通往电梯的走廊之前，我听到两声或三声短促的枪响，并看见茅小姐倒在电梯门对面的门道尽头地上。我逃进走廊，躲进建筑物内的华华 (Hwa Hwa) 杂志公司。我不知道后来发生了什么。当我在华华杂志公司时，我请求该公司的一名职员打电话给警察局报告枪击事件。在里面停留了大约10分钟后，我走出去，发现茅小姐躺在电梯旁楼梯底部的底层地面上，那时警察已经到达现场。

At 6.45 p.m. September 12, the members of the
Shanghai vocational Chinese Women's Club (上海中國職業婦女會俱樂部),
Room 203, 120 Nanking Road, held a meeting in the Canidrome,
439 Avenue du Roi Albert, some 300 persons attending.
Miss Mao Li Ying (茅麗英 ), a teacher in the Chi Siu (啟秀 )
Girls School, 634 Avenue Joffre, presided and delivered a
speech of welcome to the newly joined members. A report
was also made on the club affairs extending over the past
two months.

At 7 p.m. all persons present attended a dinner
party which was followed by a musical and stage show,
including a drama entitled "The Elder Sister Returns"
(姊姊歸來了). The play depicted the life of members of
a feudal family, how ignorant they were and how they spent
their time in religious affairs, playing mahjong, skating
and attending cinemas, all except the eldest daughter who
was patriotic and loved her country and endeavoured to
make her family contribute their money to the Government
and so do something for the nation.

At 9.30 p.m. the function concluded, when copies
of a pamphlet entitled "Vocational Women's Special Issue"
(職婦特刊 ), dated September 12, 1938, published by the
Club, were distributed among the attendance. The pamphlet
has a number of articles and include the following :-

1. Article entitled "Promote the Thrift Movement." This
article urges the women of Shanghai to advise their
relatives and friends to :-

a) avoid buying foreign and "rotten" goods.

b) promote the use of native cloth - usual Chinese cloth
is not purely Chinese product.
